SHA-256:  ac7af4de748b7e26b777f37e01cee313a308a7296a3eb080e2906b320cc55c89

Vendored for SN0 of SOFTANZA_SOUND_PLAN.md (sec.1, the vendor decision).
One header, no dependencies, all three OSs from a single source, playback
AND capture, decoders included. No cmake, no SDK.

-- TWO TRANSLATION UNITS, BECAUSE THERE ARE TWO DLLS ------------------------

The plan's FACT 3 splits the plane into a portable DSP DLL and a per-OS
device DLL. These two files make that split mechanical rather than
advisory -- the compiler enforces it, not a comment:

  stz_miniaudio_dec_impl.c   MA_NO_DEVICE_IO  -> stz_sound.dll (portable)
  stz_miniaudio_impl.c       full backends    -> stz_audiodev.dll (per-OS)

Both trim MA_NO_ENGINE / MA_NO_RESOURCE_MANAGER / MA_NO_NODE_GRAPH:
miniaudio's own high-level graph is NOT vendored. The sound graph is ours,
written in Zig on the SIMD + multicore + fft.zig tiers -- see sec.1,
"Written IN ZIG, not vendored".

-- MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (SN0, Zig 0.15.2, -O2, this machine) ---------------

Kill criterion #2 of SN0 was "if miniaudio does not compile as one TU under
zig cc with no cmake, STOP". It compiles:

    target              PORTABLE TU        DEVICE TU
    x86_64-windows      OK  11.7s  2.5MB   OK  12.4s  3.0MB
    x86_64-linux-gnu    OK                 OK
    x86_64-macos        OK                 FAIL
    aarch64-macos       OK                 FAIL

    macOS failure is exactly GLFW's: miniaudio.h:33500
        fatal error: 'CoreAudio/CoreAudio.h' file not found
    Zig bundles libc, not Apple's frameworks, and those are not
    redistributable.

Backend presence VERIFIED IN THE OBJECT FILES, not inferred from a clean
exit -- a compile that silently dropped the backends would be the false
green the plan warns about:

    linux device .o    libasound.so.2, libpulse.so.0, libjack.so.0,
                       snd_pcm_open        (ALSA/Pulse/JACK, dlopened)
    windows device .o  IAudioClient/2/3, ma_context_init__wasapi,
                       dsound.dll, winmm.dll
    portable .o        ma_decoder_init_file present;
                       ZERO device symbols

-- WHERE THIS REFINES THE PLAN ---------------------------------------------

FACT 3 assumed audio devices were "the SAME SHAPE" as GLFW windowing:
per-OS, therefore uncross-compilable. Measurement says the shape is BETTER
than that on one of the two OSs. GLFW's X11 backend needs X11/Xlib.h at
COMPILE time, so it cannot cross-compile to Linux from here. miniaudio's
ALSA/PulseAudio/JACK backends declare what they need themselves and
dlopen the .so at RUNTIME -- so the Linux device DLL cross-compiles from
this Windows box, which stz_window.dll never could.

Only macOS is genuinely blocked, and only by Apple's headers.

The two-DLL split is still right, and for its original reason: it is what
keeps stz_sound.dll buildable for every target regardless. But the device
DLL's per-OS cost is 1 OS out of 3, not 3 out of 3.

VERIFICATION STATUS, stated rather than implied:
  Windows  -- compiled here, and runtime-verified (device opened, tone
              played, buffer captured, file decoded) -- see the SN0
              RESULTS section of the plan.
  Linux    -- compiled here (cross), both TUs. NOT runtime-verified.
  macOS    -- portable TU compiled here (cross), x64 and arm64. Device TU
              needs a macOS box with the Xcode command line tools. NOT
              verified from this machine.

The file is VERSION.txt, not VERSION: a vendor-root file named VERSION on
a C include path resolves C++'s #include <version> on case-insensitive
filesystems, which broke the build once already (see vendor/stb).
